title: refactor(plugin-security): move SecurityPlugin's controlled-by-parent master relation into security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts (#25223 cut 2)
body:

_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuMYdF2uchcinMphEKW4sYxd)_

Part of #25223
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: 6353073966

Cut 2 of the `security-plugin.ts` split, as ruled in 6353073966 (letter A, narrowed). The bodies of `resolveCbpRelation` and its two loud reports, `reportCbpMasterUnresolved` and `reportRejectedReferenceAlias`, move unedited to the new module `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts`. Together they are the ADR-0055 §1 derivation of the one master a `controlled_by_parent` object takes its access from. The one module-level declaration only those bodies read, `masterNotWritableRefusal`, moves with them, and so do the two imports only it used.

It is move-only, and the card stays open for the later cuts. The amended claim is 6353132374. It supersedes the five-body claim 6352049267, whose head made `check-adr-symbol-anchors` exit 1. Branch: `claude/project-thread-3fzya4`, the harness-pinned branch for this session. It names no issue, so the claim comment is the identity record. The branch carries the withdrawn five-body commit and then the narrowing commit, and the PR's diff against its merge base `5801a4f2c` is the narrowed cut alone.

Two bodies stay in `security-plugin.ts` byte for byte, by the ruling's item 1: the read leaf `computeControlledByParentFilter` and its chain refusal `controlledByParentChainRefusal`. So do `CBP_LEAF_READ_VERBS`, `CBP_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH`, `CbpRelation` and every import they read. ADR-0055:26 `#sharingModel` and ADR-0055:58 `#controlled_by_parent` resolve only on tokens inside those two bodies. They move only after a separate Tier H docs PR repoints those anchors (ruling items 3 and 4).

## The published `.d.ts` does not change

Under the series bar (ruling 6348891160 item 1), measured on base `5801a4f2` and on the narrowed head (the tree of the commit this PR adds):

- Raw sha256 of `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts`, base and head, all four the same: `803f5bfb7da0b00f8cd8d8f25172463d8dfb07d93fbdd8a9c6f4d4b7435e429a`. The raw diff is 0 lines, so no union order moved either.
- Normalised sha256, all four the same: `b6b5c1b7fa6fa188f6e2f7e4cca3816a246b570f20d708643d116012aa86fa77`.
- The normaliser, run from `packages/plugins/plugin-security` (it sorts the members of each string-literal union and changes nothing else):

```sh
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8");process.stdout.write(s.replace(/"[^"\n]*"(?:\s*\|\s*"[^"\n]*")+/g,r=>r.split(/\s*\|\s*/).sort().join(" | ")))' dist/index.d.ts | sha256sum
```

- Positive controls on a copy of the head `dist/index.d.ts`, line 1870 (`private resolveCbpRelation;`):
  - Made public (`resolveCbpRelation;`): raw `1ff696eaab36c50ffffb459dc4a323a7b32fea15a9bd06d8cac43967ec92ac24`, normalised `41486774e365f562d279585cb6b64e282b783b7ae822bb19ef41d434a89d7a12`.
  - Renamed (`private resolveCbpRelationRenamed;`): raw `307edbdd465438d1ab2c5bcbf12d10854c3f8a4179ab90b49d065282ba6ec2ec`, normalised `5cb31db9affddd093d0068889eaef49ed684a9ab499ce213a3a77d9ebcd159ce`.
  - Both differ from the real hashes, so the comparison does see a visibility change and a rename.
- Export tables: the ESM and CJS bundles each export the same 63 names at base and head. The lists were loaded at runtime, not parsed. The sorted name list hashes `f607fd765d6b277e08b3b46ccb16d1e2d133ec55658ffe40155aef25e1bf54f0` on all four.
- The bundle JS bytes differ (`index.js` `68f4e3a8` to `6d2a398f`, `index.mjs` `1f24e6d5` to `953c5d9a`), because code moved within them.

No changeset: `skip-changeset`, per ruling 6348891160 item 4.

## What moved

Base line numbers are each method's signature at `5801a4f2`. The last column lists the members the body reads, which is exactly what its host carries.

| method | base lines | moved function async | host members |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resolveCbpRelation` | `:8884`-`:8985` | no | `cbpRelCache`, `ql`, `reportCbpMasterUnresolved`, `reportRejectedReferenceAlias` |
| `reportCbpMasterUnresolved` | `:9007`-`:9042` | no | `logger` |
| `reportRejectedReferenceAlias` | `:9094`-`:9114` | no | `logger` |

`masterNotWritableRefusal` (base `:727`-`:737`, with its docblock) moves too; `resolveCbpRelation` is its only reader. So do the two imports only it reads, `controlledByParentMasterRefusal` (with its two-line comment) and `OWD_DELEGATING_ROW_WRITES`.

## The shape (#23050 shape B, as cut 1 applied it)

- The class keeps each private method with its name, signature, docblock and position, because tsup emits private members with their JSDoc into the `.d.ts`. Each body is now one host literal plus `fn.call(host, …)`, marked `[#25223 cut 2]`.
- `CbpRelationHost` types every member as the class member itself (`SecurityPlugin['m']`). Each moved function types its `this` as the `Pick` of the host over exactly the members its body reads, and each stub annotates its literal with the same `Pick`. There is no cast, and no member becomes public or protected.
- The module imports `SecurityPlugin` type-only, so there is no runtime import cycle, and `security-plugin.ts` gains no export. `CbpRelation` is named in the module through the class's own signature (an alias over the non-null return type of `SecurityPlugin['resolveCbpRelation']`), so the interface keeps its one declaration beside `cbpRelCache` and the consumers that read it.
- The two reports go in as late-bound closures that call `this.m(...a)` on the plugin at call time. A spy or test double set on the plugin is still the one the derivation reaches. No moved body calls a function-valued field, so no receiver changes.
- Fields: `ql`, `logger` and `cbpRelCache` go as getters, because none is declared `readonly`. `start()` assigns `ql` and `logger` after construction, and the metadata watch clears `cbpRelCache` in place. The host declares every field `readonly`, so a moved body cannot assign a member through it; the typecheck passes, so none does.
- All three methods are synchronous, so no stub changes `async`. Nothing re-exports the module, so the package entry does not move.

## Proof of move-only

- **Bodies, by AST token**: for all 3 methods, the moved function's body has the same TypeScript token sequence as the base method body, and each of its 144 lines is the base line with two leading spaces removed. Parameters, return types and `async` match. A negative control, `candidates.length === 1` changed to `=== 2` in `resolveCbpRelation`, fails the check.
- **Class side**: each method keeps its docblock and signature. `masterNotWritableRefusal` is verbatim (11 lines) in the module and absent from `security-plugin.ts`. `computeControlledByParentFilter`, `controlledByParentChainRefusal` (docblock to closing brace), `CBP_LEAF_READ_VERBS` and `CBP_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` (docblock included) are byte-identical to base.
- **git's own view** (`git diff --color-moved=plain --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change 5801a4f2 HEAD` over the two source files): 158 of 159 deleted lines and 178 of 283 added lines are detected as moved.
  - Deleted, not moved (1): `OWD_DELEGATING_ROW_WRITES,`, taken out of a multi-name import. It is re-imported in the module beside `masterGovernsRowWrites`.
  - Added, not moved: the stub bodies and the import of the new module with its comment. In the module: the license header, the module docblock, the imports, the `CbpRelation` alias, `CbpRelationHost`, one pointer docblock per function and the rewritten signature heads. The rest are lines git does not pair with a moved block, such as blanks and closing braces.
- **Size**: 449 changed lines (+290 / -159, 3 files), under the 3000-line human-merge threshold. `security-plugin.ts` goes from 10,952 to 10,823 lines.

## ADR anchors (ruling 6353073966 item 2)

- `node scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs`: exit 0 at base `5801a4f2` and exit 0 at head, both with `2383 anchors across 142 records resolve — 467 symbol (440 declaration, 27 literal), 1888 file-level, 28 cross-repo, 6 exempt, 18 continuation`. CI runs this gate (`lint.yml`), but `dispatch-gates --commands` does not derive it for this change set, so it is run by hand here.
- `pnpm check:adr-anchors`: exit 0, 76 anchored files (75 at base, plus the new entry). The new entry is `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts.json`, carrying ADR-0055 and the §1 invariant paragraph of the `security-plugin.ts` entry, verbatim. That paragraph describes the master derivation, which now lives in the new module. The `security-plugin.ts` entry is unchanged, because the methods, their docblocks and both consumers of the derivation remain in that file. `docs/adr/**` is not touched.
- The anchor map covers every ADR symbol anchor naming `security-plugin.ts`: 28 anchors, 20 symbols, 10 ADRs. It was measured with `extractAnchors` and `symbolSegmentResolution` from `scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs`, which is measurement, not a new gate. Base lines are at `5801a4f2`. Every anchor resolves at head in `security-plugin.ts` with its base class, and none moves to the new module.

Only one resolving site moves: `#controlled_by_parent` at base `:9035`. It is the quoted token inside `reportCbpMasterUnresolved`'s message template, and it goes to the new module with that body, where it is still a literal. The anchor names `security-plugin.ts`, and there it keeps its other two sites. That is ruling 6353073966 premise 6, read on this cut's base.

## Readers

No test, script, gate, baseline or docs anchor reads the moved lines by path, so nothing else is re-pointed.

- The other symbol-anchor gates all exit 0: `check-scripts-symbol-anchors`, `check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:liveness`, and `check-platform-checklist --changed-from origin/main`. The last of these judged 6 anchors and lost 0.
- Line citations: no `security-plugin.ts:N` citation in the repo points into a moved range. The moved ranges are base `:727`-`:738`, `:8884`-`:8985`, `:9007`-`:9042` and `:9094`-`:9114`.

  - The citations `:132`, `:303`, `:309`, `:1614`, `:1690`, `:1736`, `:3215`, `:3281`, `:3519` and `:4344` all land in those shifted ranges. They are in `CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/launch-readiness.md`, `docs/design/predicate-compilation-convergence.md`, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` and `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`.
  - At base, every one of them already points at an unrelated line. For example, `:1614` is a middleware docblock, not the system bypass, and `:309` is `interface WriteWallRefusal`. So this cut does not make any of them wrong.

## Acceptance notes

- Nothing outside this cut is touched: no other section of the class, no behaviour, no other lane's file, and no `docs/adr/**`.
- Out of scope, noted for the seat per ruling 6353073966 items 3 and 7, and filed by the seat, not here:
  - The three ADR anchors that resolve only on tokens inside a body: ADR-0055:26 `#sharingModel`, ADR-0055:58 `#controlled_by_parent` and ADR-0123:4 `#refuseNoActiveOrganization`. They need a docs-only Tier H card.
